annotations.title: Check the numbers in a text against the file

description: Check every number in a piece of text (a report, an email, a summary, or an answer you wrote) against the spreadsheet it came from. Each number is counted again from the file and comes back as matches, counted_differently, differs (with the value the file gives) or not_checked, each with how it was counted. Use it before you send or show numbers taken from a file. Fixed rules do the reading and counting; no AI reads the text or the file. Send text, and the file as file_url (a Google Sheet shared as 'Anyone with the link', a Dropbox link, or a file in a public GitHub repository) or as file_content (CSV text, or base64 for Excel) with file_name. No account needed. The file is not stored. The text and the result are kept for 24 hours at a link that anyone with the link can open. Limits: text up to 20,000 characters and 200 numbers, file up to 10 MB, 10 checks per 10 minutes and 40 per day from one place.

content_encoding.description: How file_content is written. Default: base64 for .xlsx, .xlsm and .xls, text for everything else.

file.description: A file the person attached in ChatGPT. ChatGPT fills this in. Other assistants send file_url or file_content instead.

file_content.description: The file itself, up to 10 MB: CSV or TSV text as it is, or an Excel file encoded as base64. Send this or file_url.

file_name.description: The file's name with its extension, such as orders-october.csv or pipeline.xlsx. Needed with file_content.

file_url.description: A link to the file the numbers came from: a Google Sheet shared as 'Anyone with the link', a Dropbox link, a file in a public GitHub repository or gist, or an Every Number sample such as https://everynumber.app/samples/tickets/tickets-export-2026-10-18.csv. Send this or file_content.

sheet.description: For an Excel file with several sheets, the name of the sheet to read. Default: the sheet with the most data.

text.description: The text whose numbers should be checked, as it will be sent or shown: a report, an email, a summary, or an answer you wrote. Up to 20,000 characters and 200 numbers. Keep the sentences around the numbers; they say what each number counts.

name: verify_numbers

accuracy.description: How well this check did the last time we measured it on reports it had never seen.

expires_at.description: When the text and the result are deleted (ISO 8601). The file itself is never stored.

rows_left_out.description: Kinds of rows left out of every count unless a sentence asks for them, such as Spam or Test order.

sha256.description: Fingerprint of the file's contents. The same file always gives the same fingerprint.

numbers.description: Every number found in the text, in the order written.

at.description: Where it starts in the text, in characters from 0 (line breaks as one character, outer spaces trimmed).

context.description: The words around it, to tell apart numbers written the same way.

file_says.description: What the file gives, with how each value was counted. Filled for differs; for counted_differently it is the value on the same basis as the rest of the text.

how.description: How the written number was counted from the file. Filled for matches and counted_differently.

note.description: For differs: another way of counting that does give the written number, when there is exactly one.

text.description: The number as written in the text.

verdict.description: matches: counting the file the way the sentence says gives this number. counted_differently: the number is in the file, but on a different basis from the rest of the text. differs: the file gives another number for this sentence. not_checked: we couldn't tie it to the file; it is neither confirmed nor wrong.

result_url.description: The same result as a page: the text with every number marked, and how each was counted. Anyone with this link can open it until it's deleted.

text_scope.description: The basis the text as a whole counts on. Worked out only when several of its numbers agree with it.

also_leaves_out.description: Rows this text leaves out on top of those, such as rows where Status is Cancelled.

period.description: The period the text as a whole covers, such as Oct 12 to Oct 18.

title: Check the numbers in a text against the file
